text:
णमो अरिहंताणं
णमो सिद्धाणं
णमो आयरियाणं
णमो उवज्झायाणं
णमो लोए सव्व साहूणं
meaning: "I bow to the arihants (the awakened who still teach), to the siddhas (the liberated), to the acharyas (the leaders), to the upadhyayas (the teachers), and to all the holy ones in the world." It bows to virtues, not to any one person.
purpose: To honour the qualities of the awakened, and to cultivate them.
when: At the start of the day and before any undertaking.
note: The most fundamental prayer of Jainism. The Śvetāmbara form begins Namo instead of Ṇamo; it usually continues with a verse saying this fivefold bow destroys all wrongdoing.
source: Jain tradition; text as printed in the Wikipedia article on the Namokar Mantra
name: Navkar Mantra
iast:
Ṇamō Arihantāṇaṁ
Ṇamō Siddhāṇaṁ
Ṇamō Āyariyāṇaṁ
Ṇamō Uvajjhāyāṇaṁ
Ṇamō Lōē Savva Sāhūṇaṁ
pronunciation: na-mo a-ri-han-taa-nam; na-mo sid-dhaa-nam; na-mo aa-ya-ri-yaa-nam; na-mo u-vaj-jhaa-yaa-nam; na-mo lo-ay sav-va saa-hoo-nam
